utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Mundis, I'm informed that you would like to address the Chamber about a motion filed yesterday by the Defence. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, if I could briefly address you on that, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But if you would please do this quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: As the Chamber is aware yesterday, the Defence yesterday filed a motion seeking reconsideration of the amount time allocated to the direct examination of the expert Radinovic. The Prosecution notes in that filing or in support of the Defence position in that filing certain matters that perhaps are beyond the scope of expertise of this witness, there are matters which appear not to be covered by the Rule 65 ter summary with respect to this witness, and there are also references to videotapes which it's unclear if those are previously admitted videotapes or new videotapes, there are certainly no videotapes on the exhibit list. Leaving those matters aside, Mr. President, the Prosecution has consistently taken the position that this witness may require a significant amount of time on cross-examination and as you're well aware, we have in the past requested more time than the Defence has been allotted for direct examination. That position remains the same and if I may provide a basis for our request that we be permitted additional time beyond that for the direct examination, I point out that it will be necessary to cross-examine this witness on his lengthy statement, to cross-examine him on any issues outside the scope of that statement to which he testifies viva voce in the courtroom and it will also be necessary to cross-examine this witness with respect to the apparently large number of documents which the Defence intends to tender through this witness. So I simply raise those issues, Mr. President, so that the Prosecution position with respect to time allotted for cross-examination of this witness is clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. President. I see that the Prosecution wants more time for its cross-examination but it's not contesting the fact that we are likewise requesting more time so it seems to me that for both parties, this witness is quite important. I just like to note that the Prosecution doesn't contest the fact that we need this number of additional hours and we think that this would be useful and necessary given the issue of command responsibility. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Chamber has not had an opportunity to yet consider the matter. We'll do that as soon as possible. If there is no other issue to be -- procedural issue to be discussed at this very moment, madam usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning or should I say dobradan, Dr. Vilicic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you although it might sound superfluous in your ears that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp you may continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness please be given the document that is filed as his report in this Court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Stamp: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you not to consult any documents for the time being. We are just going to deal with two documents now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp. Although you've asked to bring the file document, unfortunately it's not there at this very moment. If the parties would --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know exactly what Mr. Stamp is referring to if he could more precise and tell us what he is referring to, this would assist us, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The Defence filed pursuant to Rule 94 bis a statement some time before it was an expert's report for this witness and two other persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: His testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are referring to the report as it has been filed in this Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could work on the basis of your copy and whenever it's on the ELMO we can check because everyone has his own copy available and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before we waste a lot of time, I'd simply like to know whether Mr. Stamp intends to develop this problem of differences between that because if that is the case then I would like to ask the expert witness to leave the courtroom and I would like to address you in order to save time for all of us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I do intend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You intend to further explore the issue you started yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As quickly as I'm allowed but I would accept my time begins when the witness returns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, madam usher, could I please ask you to escort Dr. Vilicic out of the courtroom since Mr. Piletta-Zanin ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, Mr. President, I have seen that there are differences, we have all seen that there are differences between the two maps and in the English version of the document, which is the one that was filed with the registry, I'd like to know the reason for these differences. I haven't discovered them yet but I don't think it's necessary to look for this reason for a long time. As far as I can remember from Ms. Pilipovic, I think, this witness addressed directly but we're not certain of this but I think this is what Ms. Pilipovic says, I think that he showed certain maps to the Prosecution and we weren't able to check these maps. They were given by the expert directly to the Prosecution. Perhaps there was a misunderstanding when the Prosecution and the witness were in contact or discussed matters together and it's possible that that's where the origin of the problem is but in any event, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Problem could we perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly that's what I wanted to say. The problem in our opinion is not important, because this material is preliminary material, in a certain sense anterior to the document that we elaborated. We are basing ourselves on this document if these maps mistake and let's ask the question to the witness, let's ask whether this has an affect on his final conclusions that's -- it's as simple as that in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Whatever judgement is made about whether the maps are mistaken or otherwise, whether there are changes, the reasons for the changes ought to depend on what the witness says. He's already said he prepared the English copy of the report which is filed and he prepared that from his B/C/S version he was the one who did it in respect of maps, sketches, et cetera. But what my friend is asking is that judgements be made now about things which can be easily clarified which the witness if he's asked the questions and if he answers them quickly and I don't know if it's a matter for submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean what exactly -- I now do understand that in the B/C/S versions there are maps where the confrontation lines which are very roughly put into that map are a bit different. Is that -- or is there more?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I make it very plain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version of the map, the map for incident one in Dobrinja where the Prosecution alleges that the projectile came from the east, south-east it has the confrontation line in accordance in the manner in which it is presented by the Prosecution in its evidence and in accordance with the lines on the map, the VRS map which the Defence says he uses. In the map for the second Dobrinja incident where the Prosecution says that the projectile came in from the west north-west, it moves the line in the direction of fire according to their map two to three kilometres out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you just want to clarify this -- these two maps and the lines as specifically in respect of these two incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Three incidents because there is another Dobrinja incident in which the line is brought back to the position that corresponds with the Prosecution, with the VRS map and then there are the maps which will become clear to the Court which have been filed, in which all the lines are moved away and correspond now with the lines that are with respect to incident two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I may intervene again, unless Mr. Stamp has not finished yet, I don't know, if I may intervene again, Mr. President, it's for the following reason: The error was caused directly when there was an exchange between this witness and the Prosecution. We had no control of this and this concerned our own witness. We can control the English text and that's what will be provided as evidence and everything else is additional and we are not in control of this. This is -- it's the Prosecution and the witness who were in contact so let's not waste any time. Thank you. For the English transcript, it was a sort of shadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just say that we did not meet at any time with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it must be -- you said, -- according to the translation, that it was the Prosecution and the witness who were in contact; is that what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, to the extent that -- yes, Mr. President. Yes, but it came through the registry so the intervention that I made should be changed, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Came through the office, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I've got -- the Chamber has one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, the Chamber wonders, was it by accident that the witness used this map that you noticed it or how do you know that the B/C/S version -- has it been filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It has not been filed. We requested through the Defence a copy of the B/C/S version to -- because at that time, we wanted to analyse certain things in the language in which we thought it was written originally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you noticed that there were differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Then in the analysis it was noticed that there were differences which we think should be brought to the attention of the court and the witness ought to be given an opportunity to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, it has been disclosed to you on your request.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, was it disclosed by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, we had no contact with the witness. We requested it through defence counsel and arrangements were made to have it provided to us. Maybe I could confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, that's right, Your Honour, I apologise. The witness did it directly from the Belgrade office. The witness prepared this, he came to the Belgrade office and forwarded it from Belgrade. He did this by using one of the discs that he showed us yesterday. So contact wasn't established between the witness and the Prosecution. We weren't able to control this, it was done through the office and I apologise if what I said was imprecise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stamp, you can ask questions in respect of the differences to the witness. Perhaps in order to save time, we noticed that often it takes some time to get the witness to the point you would like to ask questions about. There would be no problem in doing this in such a way that it becomes sufficient rather than --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I intend to get directly to the point because I have a huge variety of issues to go through with this witness and I would ask if the witness is not cooperative in answering - I don't like to whine and plead with the Court with regard to the witness - but I would need help that I could move on in the cross-examination in the variety of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to save time, could you perhaps ask these questions directly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I haven't seen the other maps. I do not know exactly what the differences are but if I have the feeling that intervention by the Chamber would speed up the proceedings, I certainly will intervene. Madam usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What I propose to do by starting is handing out to the Court and the parties is copies of the B/C/S maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could these be shown to the Defence counsel and a copy given to the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness I'm going to show you what I have which appears to be photocopies of the maps in your -- in the report in your original language in which I have just circled a part of the confrontation lines that you drew in red.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you give the witness a copy which is circled in red, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you put the one Slika 3.1 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have with you your original B/C/S -- when I say B/C/S I mean Bosnian/Serbian/Croatian copy of your report, do you not?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean here, you mean my copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just explain something with regard to these maps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First questions will be put to you and if there is any further explanation then needed, then of course you will be given an opportunity to do so. I will do that if necessary but please first answer Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that map on the ELMO to your right a photocopy of your figure 3.1 in your original or in the version of your report in your own language with the exception that there is a red circle around part of the line?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point to the red circle, please?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This map in your original report was in respect to incident one, the football game incident, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map relates to all the incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I explain?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I just want to confirm what they are and then you will get an opportunity to explain. Rely on me, you will have an opportunity to explain. Have -- could the witness be shown the document marked Slika 3.4. Do you -- well, firstly is that a copy of the map that was in your original version of your report?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that map is in respect to shelling incident 2?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is photograph 3.4, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was in respect of shelling incident 2?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the water line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In shelling incident 2, you understand that the Prosecution alleges that the projectile arrived from the west north-west direction.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, north-west.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you notice that the line where it is circled in red and could you point to it, please?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you notice that it has moved or it is not the same, and it has moved some distance to the west, that is, to the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, here I don't understand very well. Change between what and what? Move between what and what? Could we have the document again on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, asked you about the change in the confrontation line drawn on the one map and on the other map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Mr. President, but we were speaking about 3.4 and 3.4 then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... They are talking about the two maps shown to the witness and the maps indicate in the area of Dobrinja confrontation lines and that's what the question is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between the two that were on the ELMO earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know that these are -- you mean -- I take it that we have seen Slika 3.1 and that we are now looking at Slika 3.4, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But Mr. President, what I wish to say was that the 3.4 is exactly the same in English as we see now, so the error is an internal one I wanted to just --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is not a proper comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do not interfere in cross-examination just on the basis that you do not understand what Mr. Stamp wants to ask the witness. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at the document marked Slika 3.8. Is that a photocopy of the map that you use in your B/C/S report for your analysis of incident 4 with the exception of a red circle around part of the lines you have drawn?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the sketch of a map, this is not the map that I used, but is true that the incident number 4 is just marked here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. On this sketch -- witness, let's just confirm the basic facts then we'll move on. On this sketch of the map, do you agree with me that the line, the position of the line where it is circled in red is different from the position of the line on the map marked Slika 3.4 which refers to incident 2?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it doesn't --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't what, matter? Are you saying it doesn't matter? Is that what you said? Did you say it doesn't matter?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will get a chance to explain. Did you say it doesn't matter, Witness, that's all I'm asking?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is that this is the sketch for incident number 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. According to the scale on Slika number 8 and I'm not suggesting your scale is in any way correct, you are saying 1 kilometre is represented as 80 millimetres on this map. I suggest to you the change - that if that scale correct - moves the line of confrontation three to four kilometres in the direction of fire for incident number 2; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Incident number two in the direction that was pointed --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question I'm asking. All I want to know is if the difference in the position of the line where it is circled on Slika 3.8 when compared to Slika 3.4 in respect to incident 2 according to your scale amounts to two to three kilometres in the direction of fire for incident 2?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much, according to your scale, approximately?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This sketch has not been done in such a scale so that you can assess how far the lines are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You put a scale of 1 kilometre to 80 millimetres on 3.8, is it your evidence that that scale is meaningless?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it has no relevance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you agree with me that in the map that you have filed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you just for my clarification, Mr. Stamp, you say it moves approximately -- you said three to four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think I said two to three, I hope I said two to three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would mean that you would have it moved on the map 16 to 24 centimetres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. No, no, 16 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's 80 millimetres, 80 millimetres is 8 centimetres, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, no, I withdraw that. That is an error and I'm very grateful for your guidance, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you will agree with me that in the maps that you have filed with the English report, all of the lines for -- in respect of these three figures correspond to the lines as in Slika 3.4?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just see 3.4, please? Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said earlier that you drew your lines from the 1:50.000 VRS military map; is that your evidence that you drew the lines on the basis of a 1:50.000 scale VRS map?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1 to 5.000, I have never had such a map. 1 to 5.000?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course. Then obviously the interpretation was incorrect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I show to the witness, with your leave, Mr. President, an extract from a map already in evidence, C-2. This was a map which was disclosed by the Defence and has been indicated to being, by the Defence, as a map which the expert refers to in his the report as the one he used?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a copy of the map you used to draw your line, to draw the confrontation lines? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you see a part of it that is circled in red?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to it on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is in the vicinity of Dobrinja where the lines are also marked on the other map, other maps that I showed you.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this map, the incident number 2 took place on the Serb territory the way that this has been sketched, drawn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking simply, is that the map you used to draw your lines?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, the Chamber has been provided with -- let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Maps with and without red markings, it's a bit confusing for us. I apologise, it's the Chamber itself who marked the map. Please proceed. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just wanted to say something, that I am rather handicapped in terms of the transcript if I could have some technical assistance. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the technical booth will certainly assist you. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, notwithstanding that the lines on the VRS military map that you used are a little broad, I suggest to you that they correspond to the lines that you have used in Slika 3.8. Slika 3.8 is your original B/C/S map. Could you be shown Slika 3.8, please. Witness, you are looking at the wrong document. There it is.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this map, the enlarged map, practically incident number 2 occurred on the Serb territory which is not logical.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Stamp wait for the interpretation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have to interrupt because I want to move through this quickly, very quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suggest to you that what you are saying is not correct that according to that map that incident 2 occurred on Serb territory but all I'm asking you now: Doesn't that line in that area on that military map that you say you used correspond to Slika 3.8? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to answer because here, the map is so roughly drawn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you used this roughly-drawn map according to you, to draw your lines. I'm asking you a simple question: Does the lines, as you see them on that map which you used to draw the lines that you presented to Court, correspond with your lines in Slika 3.8?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed to answer and to explain? You won't let me answer the question. I have to explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Explain, please, I need you to answer the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First, you answer the question and then you will get an opportunity to explain, but you first should answer the question. And the question is whether the roughly-drawn line on the military map, whether that line corresponds with the line you have drawn on Slika 3.8. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it doesn't correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I suggest to you that the lines in your English report, the one that is filed, are not the correct lines of confrontation in the Dobrinja area, that you changed them to fit incident 2?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that the lines do not correspond.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well that is true, good. I'd like you to have a look at your English report. We have your English report, that is one to your right there. Please look at page 36. That page is part of your analysis of shelling incident number 2 and you will see that paragraph 2 on that page begins by saying the data presented show lack of logic and is not convincing. And you go on to catalogue what you consider areas which lack logic and are not convincing. Three lines from the end of that paragraph, you have catalogued one of the reasons why it lacks logic and is not convincing because you say, "Both the ballistic" -- I beg your pardon, "Both the official or ballistic expert reports make no mention of the position of the line of conflict." Now in light of your obvious recognition of the importance of the position of the line of conflict in respect to incident 2, would you explain to the Court of the changes which that have been made resulting ultimately in what the Prosecution submits is -- are maps with incorrect lines being presented to the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Vilicic, you now have been given an opportunity to explain so ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now explain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you were asked to explain. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In our analysis, in our expert report, as far as the distances were concerned, we used distances and ranges only from the data that was given in the official reports or other documents and we compared it to the witness statements and other statements that we couldn't take for authentic because of the subjective assessment of some witnesses who gave these statements. In all of our examinations and analyses, we never said precisely where exactly the firing position could be nor were we able to establish that. In other words, we were never able to precisely say exactly what distance was in question. We mentioned distances only from the aspect of the assessment of the angle of descent from the aspect of the impact point of the projectile. So if we're talking about incident number 2, then the assessment was carried out only on the basis of what was established on the site itself with the reports, with the on-site investigation with we agreed bearing in mind the traces on the fence, the projectile exploded above ground, that it was probably a very large angle of descent considering the number of people who were hit, and it was on the basis of that that we then proceeded to analyse from which range this projectile could have been fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you are explaining something, but you are not explaining what you were asked to explain. You were asked to explain why, on the different maps, we find different confrontation lines marked, whether it's relevant or not, whether you used it, whether you used mainly other sources is a different matter. You were asked to explain the difference in the marking of the confrontation lines on the maps. That's the only thing you were asked to explain. Would you please do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me just explain. When we handed over the Serb version on the CD-ROM together with it, we attached the four pages of these maps with the corrected lines. It is obvious that the Chamber did not receive this paper. Because there were some problems to reproduce the Serb version, I contacted the Prosecution associate by e-mail to tell her how to do this and I also said that apart from the Serb text, we have also attached four new corrected maps and I gave the pages, the pages that you're just quoting now, but I have to stress that in all of our examinations, it is not relevant this, line that I have put in, because the line has been inputted imprecisely. What I mean to say is that it doesn't correspond to reality. It had a large objective error because it wasn't our objective to actually draw that line precisely. It's been drawn as precisely to place the incident that it would be within that - for instance this incident number 2 is within the Muslim territories of course - there were no movement of lines so that we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. would get a better conclusion because we gave both maps. Here, on this CD, I have, if it is possible, I can have copies made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've heard your explanation for the change in the lines in respect to incident 2, that is on the record. Quickly, have a look at your sketch in respect to incident 3. And that's at page 40 of the filed version of your report. You may remove the B/C/S copy of your report now, we're not going to be using it until later. Page 40. Professor, you may close the B/C/S version of your report, we are dealing with the one which has been filed which you said you prepared, the English version. Thank you. Do you see where the impact spots are marked on this map?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they the correct location of the impact locations?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. The photograph is inverted, you have been given a different photograph. That's on page 40. On that CD that I'm talking about there is also this correction that's included.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. It has been inverted. And also in the report that you filed, the English version of the report that you filed and you said you checked yourself, have a look at the photograph that you used in respect to incident 2 and that is at page 35 of your report, photo number 1. Is that the photograph you used to analyse the incident?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the Skoda that was damaged as a result of the shell, that's from the official documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the original -- the photograph that you used here in court?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have it here. But just a moment, as far as I can remember, I turned this photograph around by 180 degrees so that the direction from which it was taken corresponded exactly to the position of the vehicle in the street, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit 1386. It's a recall of a document already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It saves time, Mr. Stamp, if you indicate before.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry then, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at photo 0028269707.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I said, I rotated it like this because it was more logical for me for it to be placed in that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Logical to reverse the position of the photograph so that the car appears to be east of the gate instead of west of the gate or, sorry, the car appears to be west of the gate instead of east of the gate? What is the logic in reversing the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was because the projectile came from the north and exploded -- it exploded in front of the vehicle. If you take this photograph as it is, the projectile came from the south but in the report, it states that the projectile came from the north and exploded in front of the vehicle and it hit a woman at the entrance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that you get a bit confused --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Mr.--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with the names of counsel for the Prosecution I do not. I asked Mr. [Microphone not activated] once what this means. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, you were speaking about elevations and it's the only answer I can give you but at this stage, if the Prosecution could provide us with the original negative of the photograph in question, if it has this negative so that it can be checked subsequently in order to save time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes, but let's just hear what the witness tells us. He says that his recollection is that he changed it from 180 degrees and you should not interfere at this moment. You could, during the break, or offer to say if it would be of any help we could -- but please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very quickly witness, I heard your explanation. You used this reversed photograph, did you not, in your analysis, to make or to speculate that the direction of fire could have been from the other side, from the other direction without in the report indicating in the report to the Court that you had reversed the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't change the direction, we did the opposite in order to make sure that the photograph corresponded to the direction from which the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, you have answered. May I proceed? I'm trying to move quickly; I'm not being impolite. I just wish to suggest to you that where you manipulate exhibits in a report, you ought to indicate to the persons to whom the report is addressed the manipulation and the reasons for it; would you agree with that as an expert witness?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree that I manipulated anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Vilicic, the question is the following: If you turn a photograph 180 degrees because it becomes more logic with one version of the event, that takes away, for anyone who reads the report, the opportunity to notice such an inconsistency or such an illogic difference between photograph and the version of the event. The question now is that you should do that on your own without telling those who read your report that you did it and why you did it, and whether this would not be improper to do even if you might have done it with the best intentions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this change, in my opinion, doesn't change anything with regard to the conclusions about the place where the projectile exploded and the altitude, the elevation and it doesn't change the direction from which the projectile came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Say the photograph is illogic in view of the version given to you of the event, would it not have been proper to draw the attention to this illogic rather than by turning the photograph for 180 degrees to adapt to the version of the event of the version that was presented to you it might have been of importance to this Chamber for example not to believe one of the versions that appear in not your report, but in other reports.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you have the negative of a photograph, you can print it in both ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Chamber is aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our intention was not, by any means, to change the meaning but just to make sure that the description corresponded to the position of the vehicle. It's stated that the vehicle was in front of the entrance and that Zorka Simic was standing in front of the entrance, the projectile hit her, it exploded and caused damage, deformation and given the position of the street, where the vehicle was, this photograph corresponds to the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You turned the photograph for 180 degrees because you thought that would fit better into what you had read about the cause of events; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please then move to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, quickly have a look at your sketch in respect to incident 4. That is at page 45 of your report. You said you drew those sketches yourself. Look at the impact marks on those sketches. Have you represented in your report the correct locations of the impact mark to the top left of the picture? And that is the one on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how we marked those two impacts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what basis or information did you put the impact on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Oslobodilaca Sarajeva street on that side of the street on that building?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the map of Sarajevo -- well, I found these streets in the map of Sarajevo. And as far as I can remember, it said that a projectile fell in the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva street and the other one on the surface behind the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Professor, you have presented a report which I'm sure yourself and your two colleagues took care in presenting to the Court. Are you aware that the Prosecution alleges that the impact on the building on the window frame in Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street came from the east?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well the direction of fire is indicated as being from the east. The direction of fire is from the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible for a projectile arriving from the east to hit a ground floor window or wall on that side of the street of Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the building in the Oslobodilaca Sarajeva street was possible if it came from the direction that has been indicated, why not? It is quite possible for it to hit that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not speaking of the building I am speaking of a part of the building. Are you aware that it is a the Prosecution's case that the impact on the building on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street occurred at the corner of a window and the wall of a ground floor apartment, are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the documents, that's not in dispute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where you have put this impact on Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street, look at it, is it possible for a mortar projectile -- the question is: Is it possible for a mortar projectile arriving from the east to hit the ground floor or a window of an apartment on that street, on that side of the street where you have put this impact mark?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not at all the mark for the impact on the building, this circle here doesn't refer to the window in the building being hit, it refers to the field, to the ground, the fall of the shell on the ground. The projectile hitting the window of the building couldn't have provided a basis for any assessment. One could have used it to assess the direction from which it came but it couldn't have been the basis of any other form of analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take your answers that you are representing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, I'm sorry, -- I'm sorry, I lost the line. Just a minute, please. Line 20, page 25, you said the following: "Are you aware that the Prosecution alleges that the impact on the building, on the window frame in Oslobodilaca Sarajeva Street came from the east?" Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, generally from the east. If I -- may I refer to the evidence in respect to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: No, no, it's not necessary. I wanted to be sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your explanation, witness, is that it represents a shell which fell on the ground in which case I'd like you to have a look at Exhibit P2245 -- 47, I beg your pardon. But before you do, let me ask you another question. You said that that impact mark to the top left was in reference to a -- okay, withdrawn. Have a look at the exhibit and I wish to direct your attention to photo number -- here it is, the first one 00268245 which is a photograph that you have used on your report?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the projectile that hit the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have correctly shown the angle from which it was taken on your sketch?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that the angle -- yes, according to the photograph, that would logically be the direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is correct. Please just answer the question simply, there are many points of agreement. The photograph that you examined had arrows, did it have a caption to it which you see there on the photograph, which read, "Wide angle of scene area between Oslobodilaca Sarajeva and Dz. Nehrua streets were two 120 millimetre shells landed" - I am slowing down - "nine people were killed and many wounded in the explosion, arrow marks where the shells landed."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Perhaps, Madam Registrar, a copy of Exhibit 2247.1, which is a translation of the caption could be handed to the Court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm suggesting to you, witness, is this, that a conscientious examination of the photograph which you used for your report would have indicated that both impacts on the ground were in the courtyard. If you were careful in your assessment of the evidence and the photographs, then this photograph that you have used clearly shows that both impacts on the ground were in that courtyard shown in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the report which was provided, there were two impacts in front of the underground garage and there were craters which were 97 centimetres deep which we used in the analysis and this impact in the ground was not used, or rather only a comment was made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, you don't think it is important where you put impact marks in sketches which you are presenting for the Court's consideration? It doesn't really matter what you put down there.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Quickly, the last issue I want to deal with in respect to methodology, may I take you to your -- to the English version of your report, page 46. You said in the middle of the page in the last paragraph before -- maybe I should just count it I withdraw that, you said in the middle of the page in the passage beginning, "The fact," and I will read it, "The fact that two mortar shells and one unidentified projectile have hit a site of limited dimensions within two --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down while you are reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We all go quicker if we read. Could you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "The fact that two mortar shells and one unidentified projectile have hit a site of limited dimensions within through to three minutes only can be considered accidental. If, at the distance of about 100 metres from this locality, Oslobodilaca Sarajeva number 3 (statement of Witness number 1) barracks of the Muslim forces were situated it is possible that they were the target to the weapons located in different positions at different ranges from the barracks." At page 44, in the middle of the page, you indicate Witness number 1 is Zahida Kadric, you also indicate that you analysed the statements of witness number 2, Azra Omerspahic. In your conclusions at reference 3.4, that's your conclusion at page 59, you say there is lack of reliable evidence that the locality affected was intended target of fire since military object housing Muslim forces also the dividing separating lines of the conflict were situated in close vicinity. In other words, witness, you have drawn conclusions and made statements on the basis of what Zahida Kadric is supposed to have said in her statements. The question is did Zahida Kadric say in her statement that there were military barracks 100 metres from the incident? Witness, would you prefer if I give you a copy of her statement, the B/C/S versions, original versions of her statements and after the break you can tell us whether or not she said that?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object both the fact that the Prosecution itself asked the witness not to examine his document insert and the tone seems a little rough to me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I apologise if my tone seemed a little rough. The thing is that I wanted to move through this area in 45 minutes and it has taken a little over that. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is -- I think your apologies will be accepted by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's a simple question -- well, I'm sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is that where you refer to a certain witness, whether in the statement of this witness, there appears anything about the presence of military barracks.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have all the material here, all the entire statement but the statement was such, there was such a statement. And the assumption that that could have been the target, that was concluded on the basis of the fact that shells were fired from a great distance. And in a fairly short period of time, two projectiles were fired, only these projectiles from analysed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will get into that later. I'm just trying to understand the methodology that you have used in writing, preparing, and presenting this report. You have said that on the basis of the statements of a witness who has not testified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, it's 10.30. I'd like to have a break but I would first like to ask madam usher to escort the witness out of the courtroom. We'll adjourn for half an hour, Dr. Vilicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, we can spend a lot of time on this issue but I'd like to draw your attention to two different ways of reading page 46, the paragraph you were referring to where it says, "If, at the distance of about 100 metres from this locality (Oslobodilaca Sarajeva number 3, statement of Witness number 1), barracks of Muslim forces were situated. It is possible that they were the target to weapons located in different positions," et cetera. The reference to the statement of Witness number 1 of which you said that on page 44, evidence is summarised that there were no military objects in the settlement, could be to the presence of barracks and then I fully understand what your problem is. If, however, the reference to the statement of Witness number one would refer to locality, and locality is the place where the event happened, the locality "Oslobodilaca Sarajevo number 3 statement of witness number 1," I haven't, in my mind, the statement of that witness but if the witness said that it all happened on Oslobodilaca Sarajevo number 3, then we might spend a lot of time and have a lot of confusion on a contradiction or an imprecision which might not exist. Could you please keep this in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'll keep that in mind, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could you provide the necessary instructions to the Prosecution so that we can have the negative of the photograph. We would like to check something if this is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... The Chamber if the negative of the photograph does exist then the Chamber would also be interested too but I take it that it's a picture from a report which has been delivered without negatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We do not have the negatives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in respect to the photograph that you indicated you reversed for the purpose of enhancing logic, may I suggest to you that the expert report or the investigative report of the analyst, which is in evidence before the Court, refers to a green Skoda motor car facing east and that is how it appears on the photograph which is in evidence and which is taken from the north. By your reversal, it is suggested you have put it facing west and making it inconsistent with the report of the expert. Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher, could you please put on the microphone -- your microphone is off, Dr. Vilicic, and we don't want to miss a word of you. It's on now, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at page 8 to 17 of your report, you speak about the effectiveness of mortar rounds, the likelihood of casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know whether this is important that the answers are given to the questions of the Prosecution but I clearly said -- heard what the witness said and the -- that would have to bear in the transcript so could we please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Dr. Vilicic, did I understand you well that you disagreed with which -- what was put to you by Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in calculating the probability of victims being hit, you have used certain formulas. You don't need to show him, madam usher, thank you very much. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the formulas that you used are partly based on a theoretical construct with certain assumptions including persons are spread one square metre apart on horizontal terrain; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also have indicated in your report that the that will radius of the 82 millimetre round is 18.6 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 82 and 16.1; 18.6, 120. Table 6, first row. First row.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 16.1 metres is the lethal effect for the 82 millimetre mortar and 18.6 for the 120 millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you what is the maximum distance from the explosion that the fragments can cause injury to any person who might be hit?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The effective range is the range when the energy of an impact is 100 joules per 1 centimetre square, that is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: One metre square, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And some fragments, depending on the size of the fragment and the initial velocity can go to different distances but the issue is about -- is their energy is reduced with distance so some fragments can go 50, 100 metres, but then you will not have that energy that will be sufficient to cause injury, lethal injury. A lethal injury is 100 joules per centimetre square.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like to remind you to simply answer my question. You have indicated that fragment particles can go 50 to 100 metres they can cause injury but they are not necessarily lethal. I'd like you to have a look at a sketch -- please could the witness be shown this document, this sketch. And while that is being done just for the record, you agreed that up to 100 metres the amount of particles still travelling might cause injury but not lethal injury?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some fragments, but practically speaking, from the point of view of effectiveness and calculations, standards say that 82 millimetres would be 120 metres maximum, that would be the effective range. That would be against troops and that would be --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The interpreters ask you to slow down, Dr. Vilicic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we are carrying out calculations for effectiveness, the necessary number of projectiles in order to destroy the target.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that there are a variety of calculations for different purposes. Simply you're saying 120 metres with the 82 millimetre mortar, the fragments can cause injury. How far for the 120 millimetre mortar can the fragments cause injury?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No. No, I didn't say that 82 millimetres can be 120. We had -- in practice we had one case of injury, light injury at 80 metres so it cannot go that far, the fragments do have such energy to be dispersed so far. Small fragments lose energy very quickly they have a small mass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far can fragments from the explosive burst of the 82 millimetre cause injury, what's the maximum distance; do you know?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm telling you is that according to military standards, that in calculating the range of effectiveness for 82 millimetre shell, you calculate that 20 metres and 120 millimetre shell, 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try to take away some confusion. You're talking about, Dr. Vilicic, about calculations you'd make about effectivity. Mr. Stamp is asking you what would be the maximum distance from the point of explosion where you might find injuries? I think you answered that question in respect of 82 millimetre mortars where you said that it -- that once you found a light injury at 80 metres which, as far as I understand, was relatively exceptional in your view.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So approximately the maximum where you would find even a small light injury. Could you answer that same question in respect of 120 millimetre mortars? At what distance would you possibly find someone lightly injured by a 120 millimetre mortar shell that exploded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That range is lower than the minimum range for an impact of a shell. If you have a look at the table, 120 millimetre shell, minimum range is 85 metres, and for a -- to be absolutely precise for 120 millimetre shell that would be about 100 metres or so but I would have to look at the table. Otherwise, one's own troops would be destroyed with mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What table were you referring to exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 5 for 120 millimetre mortar and page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, certainly we are talking about the distance from the point of impact so I would say it comes closer to what you described in table 6, I would say, where you say that the lethal radius is 60 metre or 80 metres but we are not talking about the radius as such but what would be the maximum, I take it that the radius is also an average of the distances on which you would still find people to be killed, what, and I'm therefore asking you where you said that you once found someone lightly injured at 80 metres by an explosion of an 82 millimetres --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Metres, metres --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think I said metres. No. 80 metres by an explosion of an 82 millimetre mortar shell, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the longest, the -- what was the greatest distance that you found from someone being injured by a 120 millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't look into this. We assess the effectiveness of a projectile in an arena and arena's radius maximum is 20 metres, the outer would be 40. It would depend on the calibre. It's an arena, you check it that segments are positioned, two or three inch planks are positioned and that's how you can assess the number of perforations and traces. These traces or scratches would mean how much this would be hit and that would be equal to an injury so it would -- that's how we would measure the effective energy and in those arenas, we never examine how far fragments could travel how far they could fly but these distances are smaller than the minimum distances that are supposed to be hit with those mortars. But because mortar is normally used from above, then -- then on the ground they are used vertically then the crews themselves would be injured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have a look at the diagram on the ELMO. Does the theoretical formula that you used to calculate hit probability take into consideration fragments like the one indicated by the arrow above the line and the arrow above the head of the man standing?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's used standing person in these analysis, that's about half a metre of width and two metres of vertical height, that's what it's used as a standard everywhere in the world for a standing figure of a man, half a metre by two metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the analysis --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't calculate anything else over that, fragments that fly over two metres are not taken into consideration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You -- would you agree with me that the positions of the persons in respect to the impact site, in reality, would be very important to factor into any assessment as to hit probability?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand. Perhaps it's a problem of interpretation. I didn't understand your question well. I'm now listening in English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If one should analyse an report upon an incident which actually happened, it is important to factor in the positions where persons are in respect to the explosion. That is, the position of the persons in relation to the site of the explosions.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, that's what's needed to be known. Yes. But in these specific situations, this was not known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we had evidence about the positions of victims in respect to each of the scheduled incidents before you submitted your report in September; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take incident number 1.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- are you aware that the football game was being played at a corner of a car park which was near to a residential building?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the ground to the east of where the impact site occurred rises up to go into the residential buildings? That the ground to the east of the impact site would be about a metre higher than the impact site itself.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that at the southern side of where the football game was being played, the ground also rises?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the evidence is that on the other side of the football game there were persons, including children, spectators, sitting atop parked vehicles watching the game?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that having regard to the difference to the relative positions of these people in that they are higher than the impact site, a theoretical formula which is based on uniform horizontal ground could not apply to predict how many people would be hit because persons in elevated positions would be within the area where they could be hit? I'd like to withdraw that question and put it one part at a time. Would you agree with me, having regard to the difference in the relative positions of the people at the football game in that they were in elevated positions as spectators, a theoretical construct based on horizontal ground would not apply to predict --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Court how it is that you would --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because what we assumed is that all the persons were on the pitch, on the level of the pitch. That means that they were practically along the lines of the pitch. That means that persons were in the least favorable position, the closest to the impact of the explosion. I think you can see that on the sketch for incident number 1 on page -- English text, let me just find it, on page 32. This rectangle, there are two rectangles, the outside rectangle represents that all the people watching the game were within this rectangle, that means that they were positioned around the pitch. That is the least favorable position considering that the shells exploded on the surface of the pitch. Much more unfavourable --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is your explanation that you assume that the victims are on the ground around the pitch at the same level or elevation as the explosion?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the least favorable situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... That couldn't apply in this particular incident. Let's look at incident 2 where you also apply this theoretical construct. Have a look at the diagram I showed you. You see --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which diagram, on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the ELMO, please. You see to the left of the diagram where I have -- where it is drawn the impact site?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your theoretical construct certainly would not take into consideration fragments which were going downward.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does take it into consideration, it's taking into consideration everything from zero to two metres of height, all the fragments, even those that ricochet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zero is the impact site on the ground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it take into consideration anything, any fragment which could be going below the ground downward?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether you understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, I am putting to you that your theoretical construct does not take into account fragments which go downward.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I have to come to the conclusion that you are not familiar with the methodology of determining the effectiveness of projectiles, to determine the effectiveness of projectiles you have to take into consideration all --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Understand to be -- by answering my questions. In your theoretical construct which includes the assumption that the shell explodes on horizontal ground, you would not take account of any fragments that would be going downward into the ground.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All fragments that ricochet are taken into account because it is by this means that you determine the density of the fragments for each projectile and that is one of the main values that is used when creating a model for calculations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which ricochet off the ground and go up, you would not take into account fragments which go down into the ground. I wonder if I'm making my --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A fragment that penetrates the ground can't be taken into account, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simply. In incident 2, are you aware that the impact occurred approximately one metre above the ground?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that it occurred at a gate leading to a yard which was further -- which was lower, much lower -- let me withdraw "much," which was lower than the street level?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Am I aware of that, yes. Not much, but about 70 centimetres, the two steps that led into the courtyard, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that many of the witnesses who testified in court were injured while they were in that courtyard which would be out of the consideration of your theoretical construct because they were below the point of explosion?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. Your conclusion is not correct. Because the calculation models include the density of fragments which is typical for each projectile, which is different for each projectile so that such a conclusion cannot be reached.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is are you aware that some of the persons who were injured in that explosion were sitting in a yard or were at a pump in a yard which was below the position of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you are forgetting the fact that the projectile exploded in the air and that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not forgetting that fact. Witness, simply, were you aware when you did your report that some of the persons injured were positioned at a lower elevation in relation to the site of the explosion? Were you aware of that when you did your report?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in the direction of the pump, only in the direction of the pump.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your answer is yes --

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a lower altitude, it's lower down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I say it that your theoretical construct and mathematical simulations would not apply to those persons who were injured?

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're forgetting the fact that we came to the conclusion that the results of ours corresponded to the number of people who were wounded and you're forgetting that fact. Have a look at table 2.5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My suggestion to you, sir, if you just answer is that your theoretical construct does not take into account the spatial distribution of fragments downward so it would not take into account the persons who were located at a lower elevation to the impact site; do you agree or do you disagree? That is all I am putting to you, witness.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree because it's completely incorrect. Our results show a greater number of people who were hit than the actual number, sir, and the number was greater than the actual number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness -- sorry, Professor, are you aware of the number of people who were inside that yard around that pump in the front yard? It's a simple question, you don't need to refer to your report, witness, let's move quickly.

utterances.speaker: JANKO VILICIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mustn't I look at the report? Am I not to look at the report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you need to look at the report to answer the question please do so and if you can do without but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just had a look to remind myself of the names of the witness who mentioned the number of people in the queue for water. Enver Taslaman in his first statement said that there were 120 men in the queue and he -- when testifying before the Trial Chamber he said there were 150.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt you witness I'm not talking about the people queueing for water that is not what the question is about, the question is about the amount of people who were in the yard with the pump. Do you know how many people were there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, Mr. Stamp, is it your position that if people are a little bit lower than ground level that you would get a higher or lower number of injured people or casualties?
